scores.evidence: take the top ~20 results from BM25 and the top ~20 from vectors, then merge them with reciprocal rank fusion
scores.rationale: All technical mechanisms (hybrid retrieval, RRF, cross-encoder rerank, embedding version tracking, retrieval-time visibility filters) are described accurately with no false claims about guarantees or vendor behavior.

scores.evidence: Account-specific actions like refunds, order lookups or password resets. Those need authenticated tool calls and belong in phase 2.
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities with explicit open questions, and excludes scope with reasons; the phased build is realistic for a small team.

scores.evidence: if you index agent-only content later, enforce visibility filters at retrieval time, not in the prompt
scores.rationale: Components, data flows and ownership are consistent end to end; decisions like grounding, visibility filtering and PII redaction are honored uniformly across ingestion, retrieval, generation and logging.

scores.evidence: Run evals in CI on any change to prompts, chunking or models.
scores.rationale: A golden set from real tickets with retrieval, faithfulness and refusal metrics, adversarial cases, CI regression gating, internal beta, A/B test and production feedback loop target the riskiest assumptions before and after launch.

scores.evidence: this plan uses common defaults and marks the choices that depend on your answers. The open questions are at the end.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit, numbers are ranges or marked rough, and the open-questions list ties each unknown to what it would change (e.g., volume drives cost and latency choices).

scores.evidence: Hallucinated policies (refunds, pricing) | Strict grounding, citation checks, confidence gate, escalation for policy topics
scores.rationale: The major domain failures (hallucination, stale docs, injection, retrieval misses, user frustration) have concrete detection and mitigation, but abuse/rate limiting and LLM-provider outage or degradation are not covered.

scores.evidence: Weekly review dashboard: top unanswered and low-confidence questions.
scores.rationale: Logging, meaningful dashboards, CI gating and staged rollout are concrete and sized to a small team, but deployment/rollback mechanics, incident ownership and on-call are not addressed.

scores.evidence: Cache frequent Q&A, use a smaller model by default, cap context size
scores.rationale: Concrete cost controls and per-turn token-cost logging are included, but there is no cost-per-conversation estimate, scaling reasoning or build-cost consideration even as an order of magnitude.

scores.evidence: record the model version on each chunk so you can re-embed later
scores.rationale: Hard-to-change choices are isolated (re-embed path, index chosen from whatever you already run, tool access deferred), though reversibility is not reasoned about explicitly for the data/metadata schema or vendor coupling.

scores.evidence: Extras worth adding: Generate 3–5 synthetic questions per article
scores.rationale: The pipeline is close to the simplest workable design for multi-turn support RAG; every component is justified by a need (BM25 for error codes, rewrite for follow-ups) and enhancements are labeled optional with a growth path.

scores.evidence: 1. Prototype | 2 weeks | Ingestion, hybrid retrieval, basic chat, first eval set; offline retrieval recall@5 of at least 85%
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered by dependency with checkable deliverables and specific decisions (chunk sizes, metadata schema, top-k, fusion), leaving only stack selection pending the user's answers.
